- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.22) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.11) over 3+ days, model may overfit upward trend; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for next 5 days.
- Mean reversion is triggered if 3 consecutive forecast days are >+2% above true outcome; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >+5% above 18-day moving average, model often underestimates; add +1–2% to forecast for next 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 for 3+ days), model tends to lag; forecast should be 0.5–1.5% higher than true outcome for next 5 days.
